experiment: ablations (redesigned around what is actually ablatable)

analysis.significance_test: McNemar exact test against full_model, p < 0.05

notes.uniform_weights: No-op ablation. With geometric scoring there is no trained head and outcome weights at inference are always 1.0, so it is reported at the full-model number with this explanation rather than as a measured delta.
notes.k_sweep: Varying k is not a valid ablation: k is inert for k >= top_k (3). Accuracy was identical (33.6%) at k=5, 10, 20 and 50 on the full store.
notes.random_fusion: 3 neighbours chosen uniformly at random (seed 42, without replacement) and fused with the same renormalised weighting; only the selection differs from the full model.
notes.no_navigation: Retrieval skipped; navigate() receives concat([query_vector, zeros(256)]), so endings are scored against the raw query position.
notes.single_neighbor: fuse_directions(top_k=1): follow only the strongest memory.

architectural_findings.k_inert: k is inert for k >= top_k (=3). Accuracy identical from k=3 to k=100. Navigation direction determined by top-3 regardless of retrieval pool size.
architectural_findings.outcome_weights: Geometric scoring uses no trained head, so outcome weights at inference are always 1.0. Training-time outcome weighting was superseded by the architecture change in Task 8.
architectural_findings.hyperedge_bonus: Not implemented. Left for future work.
architectural_findings.navigation_direction: Measured, not assumed: removing navigation entirely (no_navigation) scores 37.6% vs the full model's 33.6% (delta +4.0%, McNemar p=0.0953). Moving the position toward the retrieved-memory neighbourhood does not help on this task; the strongest single geometric signal is the cosine similarity between the candidate ending and the context position itself.
